result.topic_en: Calculations toward the Riemann–Siegel approach for the zeta function: the Euler product, the Mellin-integral representation of zeta via the theta-type function psi(x) and its functional equations, and saddle-point (stationary phase) computations for an integrand of the form $e^{-\pi x} x^{ti/2+1/4}$.
result.transcription:
$\zeta(s) = \Sigma \frac{1}{n^s} = \Pi(1-\frac{1}{p^s})$ \quad $\int_0^\infty e^{-nn\pi x} x^{\frac{s}{2}-1}\partial x = \frac{\Pi(\frac{s}{2}-1)}{n^s}\pi^{-\frac{s}{2}}$
$\Pi(\frac{s}{2}-1)\pi^{-\frac{s}{2}}\zeta(s) = \int_0^\infty \psi(x)\, x^{\frac{s}{2}-1}\partial x = \frac{2}{s}\int_0^\infty \psi'(x)\, x^{\frac{s}{2}}\partial x$
$2\psi(x)+1 = (2\psi(\frac{1}{x})+1)\, x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ \quad $\psi(x+2i) = \psi(x)$
$2\psi(x+i)+1 = (\psi(\frac{1}{4x}) - \psi(\frac{1}{4x}+i))\, x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$
[-$2\psi'(x)$ ...-]
$2\psi'(x) = -x^{-\frac{3}{2}}(\psi(\frac{1}{x})+\frac{1}{2}) - 2\psi'(\frac{1}{x})\, x^{-\frac{5}{2}}$
$-\frac{1}{s}\int (x-2n\pi i)^{-\frac{3}{2}} x^{\frac{ti}{2}+\frac{1}{4}}\partial x$
$-\frac{3}{2}\log(x-2n\pi i) + \log x\, \frac{ti}{2}$
$2\psi(\frac{1}{y}+2\nu i)+1 = y^{\frac{1}{2}}(2\psi(y)+1)$
$\int (\frac{1}{y}+2n\pi i)^{\frac{ti}{2}-\frac{1}{4}} (y^{-\frac{1}{2}}(\psi(y)+1) + y^{\frac{1}{2}}2\psi'(y))\, dy$
$\frac{ti}{2}-\frac{1}{4}\log(\frac{1}{y}+2n\pi i) - \frac{1}{2}\log y + \log(1+\psi(y)+2y\psi'(y))$
$(\frac{ti}{2}-\frac{1}{4})\frac{1}{\frac{1}{y}+2n\pi i} - \frac{1}{4y} - \frac{1}{2}\frac{1}{y} + \frac{3\psi'(y)+2y\psi''(y)}{1+\psi y+2y\psi' y}$
$\frac{ti}{2}$ \quad $\pi\pi\, e^{-\pi y} - \frac{1}{4yy} = 0$
$-\pi y = -2\log 2\pi y$
$4x = 4\log x$ \quad [-$4x = \log x$-]
$1-\frac{4}{x}$
$x=4$
$\frac{4}{4} r\cos\varphi = \log r$ \quad $4\, 1 - \log 4$
$\frac{4}{4} r\sin\varphi = \varphi$
$r = $ [-...-] \quad $r = \frac{\varphi}{4\sin\varphi}$
$\varphi\cot\varphi = \log\frac{4\varphi}{4\sin\varphi}$
$-\frac{1}{\varphi} + 2\cot\varphi - \varphi(1+\cot\varphi^2) = -\frac{1}{\varphi}((1+\varphi\cot\varphi)^2 + \varphi\varphi)$
$-\pi\; e^{-\pi x} x^{\frac{ti}{2}+\frac{1}{4}}$
$-\pi x + \frac{ti}{2} + \frac{1}{4} = 0$
$x = \frac{ti}{2\pi} + \frac{1}{4\pi}$
